metadata.note: The Overland Route as it actually ran in the twentieth century - the single busiest passenger corridor the map was missing. data/first_transcontinental_railroad.geojson draws the 1869 line and stops in 1942, when the original Promontory Summit segment was scrapped for the war effort, so between 1942 and Amtrak in 1971 the map had no line at all through Reno, Elko, Cheyenne or North Platte - even though the Overland Limited, the City of San Francisco, the Challenger and the City of Los Angeles all ran here daily. This layer draws the post-1904 alignment: Union Pacific Omaha - Ogden and Southern Pacific Ogden - Oakland over the Lucin Cutoff, 1904 to Amtrak. It deliberately overlaps the existing first-transcontinental layer for 1904-1942, because the two are different alignments over the Great Salt Lake - Promontory Summit versus the Lucin causeway - and the older layer’s geometry is a schematic town-to-town approximation while this one is traced from OSM. The Chicago - Omaha leg (Chicago and North Western to October 30 1955, Milwaukee Road after) is not drawn here.
geometry_sources: Traced from OpenStreetMap route relations pulled whole from the OSM API and stitched into one graph at their closest node pairs. Omaha - Ogden: 2280868 UP Omaha Subdivision, 7524286 Columbus, 7430259 Kearney, 8912095 North Platte Terminal, 7129340 Sidney, 7429476 Laramie, 7429530 Rawlins, 7429637 Evanston and 5407633 Ogden subdivisions. Ogden - Oakland: 8805633 Lucin Cutoff, 1521602 Lakeside, 4766672 Shafter, 1521601 Elko, 4766671 Nevada, 4489569 Roseville and 4493104 Martinez subdivisions. Dijkstra between terminals, Douglas-Peucker at 20 m.
not_yet_sourced: No Union Pacific or Southern Pacific timetable was consulted for this layer. Every avg_speed_kmh is derived from the City of San Francisco’s overall Chicago - Oakland schedule, and every headway_min is an estimate - the route carried several daily trains each way in its prime, not the one this file’s 1440 implies.

The Chicago - Omaha leg of the Overland Route is not drawn: the Chicago and North Western line to 1955 and the Milwaukee Road line after it are both absent from the map, so the corridor as drawn starts at Omaha.

Amtrak’s San Francisco Zephyr (June 11 1972 - July 15 1983) ran Chicago - Denver - Ogden - Oakland, using the Union Pacific between Denver and Ogden rather than the Omaha line drawn here. Its Denver - Cheyenne leg is not drawn anywhere on the map, and the train itself is not drawn.

The exact year the Union Pacific line east of Ogden reached its present alignment is not checked segment by segment; 1904 is used as the start year for the whole route because that is when the Lucin Cutoff changed the route as a whole.
metadata.passenger_only_rule: Both features end in 1971 with the Amtrak transition, not with the railroad: Union Pacific still runs freight over all of it. Amtrak service since 1971 - the City of San Francisco to June 1972, the San Francisco Zephyr to 1983 and the California Zephyr since - is drawn in data/amtrak.geojson.

properties.speed_source: Estimated from the City of San Francisco’s 39h45 Chicago - Oakland schedule of 1936 (about 92 km/h over the whole 2,270-mile run) knocked down for the slower trains that shared the line; no Union Pacific timetable for this segment alone was consulted.

segments.note: The Overland Route in its post-Lucin form. The Lucin Cutoff - 102.9 miles of new line from just west of Ogden straight across the Great Salt Lake to Lucin, opened 1904 - took 43.8 miles, 3,919 degrees of curvature and 1,515 feet of climb out of the route and left the original 1869 line through Promontory Summit as a branch. The Overland Limited, renamed from the Overland Flyer on November 17 1895, was the route’s flagship. headway_min is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the 1904 Lucin Cutoff, its 102.9-mile length and the 43.8 miles / 3,919 degrees / 1,515 feet it saved, the 1,029-mile Omaha - Ogden distance and the November 17 1895 renaming of the Overland Flyer to Overland Limited are all from the Wikipedia Overland Route article. headway_min is an estimate.

segments.note: Streamliner era: the City of San Francisco began June 14 1936, running Chicago - Omaha - Ogden - Oakland in 39 hours 45 minutes each way, with the Chicago and North Western handling Chicago - Omaha, the Union Pacific Omaha - Ogden and the Southern Pacific Ogden - Oakland. The Overland Limited ran alongside it. headway_min 1440 counts one City of San Francisco each way; the route carried several other trains besides.
sources: Segment-level: the June 14 1936 inaugural and the 39h45 schedule are from the Wikipedia City of San Francisco article; the C&NW’s role from the Overland Route article.

segments.note: The Chicago and North Western gave up the Chicago - Omaha leg to the Milwaukee Road on October 30 1955. The Overland Limited made its last run on January 2 1963. Union Pacific and Southern Pacific passenger operation ended with Amtrak on May 1 1971; Amtrak kept a City of San Francisco going until June 1972.
sources: Segment-level: the October 30 1955 switch from the C&NW to the Milwaukee Road and the January 2 1963 end of the Overland Limited are from the Wikipedia Overland Route article; the May 1 1971 Amtrak transition and Amtrak’s continuation of the City of San Francisco into June 1972 are from the Wikipedia City of San Francisco article.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from nine UP subdivision relations: 986 traced miles against the 1,029 miles the Overland Route article gives for Omaha - Ogden, about 4 per cent short - the trace starts at the Omaha end of the relation rather than at the Council Bluffs station the mileage is measured from. Passes within 2 km of Fremont, Grand Island, North Platte, Sidney, Cheyenne, Laramie, Rawlins, Green River and Evanston. One 5.0 km straight-line join was needed where two OSM relations do not touch; everything else is on real track. Long straight legs of up to 38 km are the Douglas-Peucker simplification of genuinely straight Nebraska and Wyoming tangents, not invented geometry. This is the present-day alignment - the 1869 line through Promontory Summit is a different route and is drawn, schematically, in data/first_transcontinental_railroad.geojson. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 9 ruled segments totalling 158 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: The Overland Route in its post-Lucin form. The Southern Pacific had leased the Central Pacific’s operations since 1885, so this half of the route was Southern Pacific-run throughout the era drawn here.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from seven relations including the Lucin Cutoff itself (OSM 8805633): 776 traced miles Ogden - Oakland, against a route the Overland Route article describes as 43.8 miles shorter than the pre-1904 line. The trace passes within 1.3 km of Lucin and within 0.5 km of Wells, Elko, Winnemucca, Lovelock, Reno, Truckee, Colfax, Sacramento and Martinez - and stays 50 km away from Salt Lake City and Wendover, confirming it follows the Southern Pacific over the lake rather than the ex-Western Pacific line to the south. Four internal gaps of 6-10 km where the OSM relations do not touch are bridged with straight lines, the longest 9.5 km near Lovelock. Long straight legs are Douglas-Peucker simplification of real tangents. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 6 ruled segments totalling 116 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).
